fine_lines.title: dial down vs crank up
fine_lines.explanation_ar: dial (something) down = يخفّف شدّة شيء (صوت، حماس، انتقاد). crank (something) up = يزيد شدّة شيء (صوت، ضغط، حرارة). هما عكس بعضهما.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Dial (something) down' = reduce the intensity of something (noise, excitement, criticism). 'Crank (something) up' = increase the intensity (volume, pressure, heat). They are opposites.

examples.sentence: Can you dial down the TV? The baby is sleeping.
The exam date moved forward, which cranked up the pressure.

fine_lines.title: rope someone in vs sound someone out
fine_lines.explanation_ar: rope someone in(to doing something) = تُقنع شخصاً بالمساعدة في شيء لا يريده كثيراً. sound someone out = تحاول معرفة رأي شخص بطريقة غير مباشرة قبل اتخاذ قرار.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Rope someone in (to doing something)' = persuade someone to help, often when they don't really want to. 'Sound someone out' = find out what someone thinks, often indirectly, before you decide.

examples.sentence: My sister roped me into painting her kitchen.
Let's sound out the teacher before we plan the trip.

fine_lines.title: dabble in vs level up
fine_lines.explanation_ar: dabble in something = تمارس شيئاً بشكل خفيف وغير جدي. level up = تحسّن شيئاً ليصل إلى مستوى أعلى أو مساوٍ لغيره (من ألعاب الفيديو).
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Dabble in something' = do it casually, not seriously. 'Level up' = improve something to a higher level or to the same level as others (from video games).

examples.sentence: I dabble in photography at weekends.
This course will help you level up your English.

expressions.meaning_ar: يمارس شيئاً بشكل خفيف وغير جدّي
expressions.meaning_en: to do something casually, not very seriously
expressions.example: He dabbles in cooking but mostly eats out.

expressions.meaning_ar: يُقنع شخصاً بالمساعدة في شيء لا يرغب فيه كثيراً
expressions.meaning_en: to persuade someone to help, often when they don't want to
expressions.example: I got roped into organising the school trip.

expressions.meaning_en: to reduce the intensity of something
expressions.example: Let's dial down the arguing and find a solution.

expressions.meaning_ar: يبتكر فكرة أو خطة (أو عذراً)، غالباً بسرعة أو بذكاء
expressions.meaning_en: to invent an idea, plan or excuse, often quickly or cleverly
expressions.example: We cooked up a plan to surprise our teacher.

expressions.meaning_ar: يستطلع رأي شخص قبل اتخاذ قرار
expressions.meaning_en: to find out what someone thinks before you decide
expressions.example: I'll sound out my parents about the trip first.

expressions.meaning_ar: يرتقي أو يُحسّن شيئاً إلى مستوى أعلى أو مساوٍ لغيره
expressions.meaning_en: to improve something to a higher level or to the same level as others
expressions.example: The school wants to level up its science labs.

expressions.meaning_en: to explain or show someone something step by step
expressions.example: Can you walk me through the new app?

expressions.meaning_en: to increase the intensity of something
expressions.example: They cranked up the heating because it was so cold.

grammar.title: Separable phrasal verbs
grammar.explanation_ar: كثير من الأفعال المركّبة تنفصل: يمكن وضع المفعول بعد الحرف أو قبله: crank up the volume / crank the volume up. أما الضمير (it, him, me) فيجب أن يأتي في الوسط: crank it up، rope me in، walk him through (وليس crank up it). لكن dabble in لا تنفصل: dabble in art.
grammar.explanation_en: Many phrasal verbs are separable: the object can go after or before the particle: crank up the volume / crank the volume up. A pronoun must go in the middle: crank it up, rope me in, walk him through. 'Dabble in' is not separable: dabble in art.
examples: Dial down the TV. / Dial the TV down. / Dial it down.
